FRBRname.value: Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959 (section 138 fees, Article 21)

note.p: Article 21 of Schedule II to the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959 (Act 10 of 1960), as inserted by the Kerala Finance Act, 2024, with effect from 1 April 2024 (Kerala Finance Bill 2024, Chapter II, para 3). Sets the court fee on a section 138 complaint, appeal and revision. Note: the slabs were subsequently revised by the Kerala Finance Act, 2025 - verify the current schedule before relying on the figures.

longTitle.p: KERALA COURT FEES AND SUITS VALUATION ACT, 1959 (SECTION 138 FEES, ARTICLE 21)

article.heading: Court fees on complaints, appeals and revisions under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881

item.p: Application or petition containing a complaint or charge of an offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (Central Act 26 of 1881)-
if the amount of the dishonoured cheque involved in the complaint does not exceed ten thousand rupees - Two hundred and fifty rupees.
if the amount of the dishonoured cheque involved in the complaint exceeds ten thousand rupees - Five percent of the entire cheque amount, subject to a maximum of three lakh rupees.
Memorandum of appeal under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881-
where the appeal is filed by the accused before the Sessions Court - One thousand rupees.
where the appeal is filed by the complainant before the High Court - An amount equivalent to one half of the court fees paid in the trial court.
Revision petition presented to the High Court-
filed by the complainant challenging insufficiency of sentence - One tenth of the cheque amount.
filed by the accused against conviction - One thousand and five hundred rupees.
